target_customer: Equipment rental firms, film and TV productions, construction, events and telecom operators needing portable power
problem: Diesel generators are noisy and polluting but are the default portable power for job sites and film sets; there was no scaled battery alternative.
business_model: Hardware sales and rental fleet supply of mobile battery energy storage units, with major rental company channel partners

founders.name: Paul Huelskamp
founders.background_notes: Sources conflict on the founding team: other pages name Alexander Meek and Jed Mickle.

founders.name: Alexander Meek
founders.background_notes: Per his YC profile, a venture investor; claims about revenue and funding raised are self-reported.

exit.reason: CEO said the company had not found a path that would allow it to continue operations; Chapter 7 filed August 2024

technical_complexity.rationale: Designing and manufacturing high capacity (about 600 kWh) mobile battery systems with safety, thermal management and power electronics, then scaling to hundreds of units, is hardware heavy for a startup.

defensibility.rationale: Battery cells and power electronics are commodity inputs; moat relied on manufacturing scale and customer contracts. Generac and hybrid system vendors could enter and did sell battery units.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Generac later sold a mobile battery unit. Moxion itself failed in 2024 and its California production facility was bought by Viridi Parente.

market_need_then: Regulations and corporate pledges to cut diesel use, plus strong interest from Amazon Studios and rental companies; Sunbelt Rentals made a multiyear purchase commitment and Amazon began powering sets with Moxion units.

branding.domain_note: Uses moxionpower.com, with Power appended to the brand.

identity.voice_and_tone: Tagline reported by a profile page: 'Good Energy. Radical Power.' (not confirmed from a primary source)

branding.community_and_virality: Amazon Studios publicly highlighted use of Moxion units on TV and film sets, a form of third party brand exposure.

brand_strength.rationale: Distinctive coined name with strong customer logos (Amazon, Sunbelt), but no sourced evidence that the brand itself drove growth.

outcome_analysis: Moxion raised a 10 million Series A in May 2021 and a 100 million Series B in September 2022 backed by Amazon, Microsoft and Sunbelt, and grew to about 400 employees. After layoffs in June 2024 it closed on July 26, 2024 and filed Chapter 7 in August. Press and insider accounts say it scaled production before resolving technical problems and relied heavily on a few early customers, while the company cited funding and investor challenges; the exact cause is only partly public.
notes: Unverified: an 11M round dated June 2023 at 745.74M post money appears only on Forge (aggregator); totals range from 110M to 250M across sources. Company site returned HTTP 503 at fetch time. Competitor list empty: the search found only 2022 to 2025 coverage of Zenobe, Generac, Kore Power and Allye, none dated near early 2021. Founder names conflict across sources. Series A date from the May 2021 release; leading investor per search result summary.
